newsitem.title: UK: UK bank customers still wary of account switching.
newsitem.headline: UK bank customers still wary of account switching.

text.p: British bank customers, traditionally loyal to their bank despite sometimes questionable service, are still suspicious of switching their accounts, according to a banking survey published on Tuesday by Abbey National.

The Abbey, the country's second biggest mortgage lender, said over half of a representative sample of 4,000 people said changing their account to another bank or building society would cause too much hassle and inconvenience.
This is despite the fact that 26 percent of current account customers in Britain -- around 16 million of the 61 million chequing accounts in the country -- still receive no interest on their money.
The Abbey said this equates to an estimated 130 million stg loss of potential interest every year.

But many of those that do get interest are not very happy. Just under a third of the sample said they are dissatisfied with the rate they are getting. Customers also complained of shoddy service, errors on their accounts and service charges.

"This survey shows that, unlike other shopping decisions such as food or clothes, customers are not shopping around for a bank account that is cheaper to run and which would ultimately save them a lot of money," said Andrew Pople, head of Abbey's retail division.
The bank said the survey findings pointed to a potential of nearly two million customers seriously considering switching banks.

It predicts that as competition in the financial services industry intensifies and results in better service and lower charges, customers will become more and more aware of better alternatives to their existing account.
